answer: Each epoch, every agent's reputation ledger is scored by a grading panel drawn by verifiable random beacon from the full pool, so no attacker knows in advance which jade-standard jurors will judge their submissions. Sybil identities must stake deposits to join, and since panels rotate before collusion can form, buying influence means corrupting a new random slice every epoch, costing more than honest work earns. A tundra of cheap fake accounts simply never accumulates enough epochs of good grades to matter.
